lede: The surah the Prophet ﷺ recited from the pulpit on Fridays, so often that a woman of Madinah learned it by heart from his mouth alone. It follows one human being from his whispered thoughts to his deathbed, to the Trumpet, and to the moment he is told: today your sight is sharp.

names.name: Qāf
names.note: The single letter it opens with. The Companions called it Qāf, or Qāf wa-l-Qurʾāni l-majīd.

names.name: al-Bāsiqāt
names.note: A name Ibn al-Jawzī records, from its tenth ayah: “and tall palm-trees, with clustered spathes.”

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah, Qatādah and the majority. One ayah is related from Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah to be Madinan: the thirty-eighth, which says that no weariness touched Allah in creating the heavens and the earth. Ibn Kathīr notes that this surah is, on the sound view, the first of the Mufaṣṣal — the last and most often recited portion of the Qurʾan.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ ق وَيُقالُ لَها: سُورَةُ الباسِقاتِ رَوى العَوْفِيُّ [وَغَيْرُهُ] عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أنَّها مَكِّيَّةٌ، وكَذَلِكَ قالَ الحَسَنُ، ومُجاهِدٌ، وعِكْرَمَةُ، وقَتادَةُ، والجُمْهُورُ
وَهَذِهِ السُّورَةُ هِيَ أَوَّلُ الْحِزْبِ الْمُفَصَّلِ عَلَى الصَّحِيحِ، وَقِيلَ: مِنَ الْحُجُرَاتِ

setting: What astonished Quraysh, the surah says at once, was two things together: that a warner should come to them from among themselves, and what he warned of. “When we are dead and have become dust? That is a far-fetched return.” The whole of Qāf is the reply.

It replies first from above and around them — the sky with no rift in it, the earth spread out, the rain that brings dead land to life: “such is the coming forth.” Then from history, in a rapid roll-call of eight peoples who said the same thing. Then it moves in, closer than any of that, to the person himself. “We created man, and We know what his own soul whispers to him; and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.” Two angels sit, one on his right and one on his left; he does not utter a word but a watcher is ready beside him.

From there the surah does not leave him. The stupor of death arrives “in truth — that is what you used to shrink from.” The Trumpet. Every soul comes with one to drive it and one to bear witness. And the sentence that gives the surah its force: “You were heedless of this; now We have removed your covering from you, and your sight today is sharp.”

The Prophet ﷺ made this the regular matter of his Friday address, and recited it in the great gatherings of the two ʿĪds. Ibn Kathīr explains why: it holds the beginning of creation, the Resurrection, the Reckoning, the Garden and the Fire, promise and threat.

occasions.title: “No weariness touched Us”
occasions.text: The commentators relate that this ayah answers the claim that after creating the heavens and the earth in six days the Creator rested on the seventh. “We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no weariness touched Us.”
occasions.source: Reported from Qatādah and others; it is why some held this one ayah to be Madinan.

aim: To awaken heedless hearts, so that they grasp the realities of the Resurrection and the Recompense — its proofs, and its scenes.

outline.title: Their astonishment
outline.summary: Qāf. By the glorious Qurʾan. They marvel that a warner has come to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers say: “This is a strange thing. When we have died and become dust? That is a distant return.” We know what the earth takes of them, and with Us is a Book that preserves.

outline.title: Look up, and around
outline.summary: Have they not looked at the sky above them — how We built it and adorned it, and it has no rifts? And the earth: We spread it out, cast into it firm mountains, and made every lovely kind grow in it. We sent down blessed water from the sky and grew by it gardens, grain for harvest, and tall palms with clustered fruit — and gave life by it to a dead land. Such is the coming forth.

outline.title: Those who denied before
outline.summary: Before them the people of Nūḥ denied, and the people of al-Rass, and Thamūd; ʿĀd, Pharaoh and the brothers of Lūṭ; the people of the Thicket and the people of Tubbaʿ. All denied the messengers, and My threat came true. Were We wearied by the first creation? No — yet they are in doubt about a new creation.

outline.title: One person, from thought to Trumpet
outline.summary: We created man and know what his soul whispers to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein. Two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left; he utters no word but there is a watcher by him, ready. The stupor of death comes in truth. The Trumpet is blown. Every soul comes, with it a driver and a witness. “You were heedless of this; We have lifted your covering from you, and your sight today is sharp.”

outline.title: Before the Judge
outline.summary: His companion says, “This is what I have ready.” “Cast into Hell every stubborn disbeliever, hinderer of good, transgressor, doubter.” His other companion says, “Our Lord, I did not make him transgress; he was himself far astray.” He will say: “Do not dispute before Me. The word is not changed with Me, and I am not unjust to My servants.” The Day We say to Hell, “Are you filled?” and it says, “Is there more?”

outline.title: The Garden brought near
outline.summary: The Garden is brought near to the mindful, not far off: “This is what you were promised — for everyone who turned often to Allah and kept his duty, who feared the Most Merciful unseen and came with a heart turned in devotion. Enter it in peace.” They will have whatever they wish there — and with Us is more.

outline.title: A reminder for whoever has a heart
outline.summary: How many a generation We destroyed before them, mightier than they. In that is a reminder for whoever has a heart, or lends an ear while he is present in mind (50:37). We created the heavens and the earth in six days, and no weariness touched Us. So be patient with what they say, and glorify your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and in the night. You are not a tyrant over them: so remind, by the Qurʾan, whoever fears My threat.

keyAyah.why: The ayah that removes every distance between the Creator’s knowledge and a person’s most private thought.

virtues.text: “I did not learn ‘Qāf, by the glorious Qurʾan’ except from the tongue of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he used to recite it every Friday on the pulpit when he addressed the people.”

ʿUmar asked Abū Wāqid al-Laythī what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite in the prayers of al-Aḍḥā and al-Fiṭr. He said: “He used to recite in them ‘Qāf, by the glorious Qurʾan’ and ‘The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split’.”
“Hell will go on saying, ‘Is there more?’ until the Lord of Might places His Foot in it; then it will say, ‘Enough, enough, by Your might,’ and its parts will draw together.”
virtues.arabic: لاَ تَزَالُ جَهَنَّمُ تَقُولُ هَلْ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ حَتَّى يَضَعَ رَبُّ الْعِزَّةِ فِيهَا قَدَمَهُ

before: Al-Ḥujurāt, the last of a group of Madinan surahs, ended on Allah’s knowledge of the unseen. With Qāf the muṣḥaf returns to Makkah and to the unseen itself — and the Mufaṣṣal begins.
after: Qāf ends: remind, by the Qurʾan, whoever fears My threat. Al-Dhāriyāt opens with an oath that what you are threatened with is true.
